7. Defendants further contended that in the absence of prayer for recovery of possession of the property, the suit was hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and the suit was further barred by limitation under Article 120 of the Limitation Act. 

 8. The learned Subordinate Judge dismissed the suit holding inter alia, that the suit as framed was not maintainable and that it was barred by limitation. On question of title the trial Court held that the plaintiffs were not 16 annas owners of the suit property. 

 b) Whether the suit is barred under Article 120 of the Limitation Act, the suit being filed beyond six years after accrual of cause of action. 

 13. The learned Counsel further argued that the question of limitation had also been erroneously decided by these two Courts ignoring, the provision of Article 120 of the Limitation Act. The learned Counsel submits that since the appellant M/s. Jute Trading Corporation Co. Ltd., has been in actual possession of the suit premises, which has also been admitted by the plaintiffs, a suit for mere declaration without prayer for recovery of possession is wholly infructuous and hence the present suit cannot be maintained. It is further submitted that a declaratory decree cannot be put into execution and to recover possession, a decree for possession by a competent Court is necessary. It is argued that the High Court Division was manifestly wrong in holding that mere declaration is sufficient. 

 14. On the point of limitation, the learned Counsel argues that the cause of action, if any, for the present suit first arose on 8.4.67 when the suit property vested in the Government as per notification No. SRO 786 (K) 167 of the then Government of Pakistan and Article 120 of the Limitation Act is the relevant article applicable to the case. The suit has been filed beyond 6 years after accrual of the cause of action. Limitation commences to run from the date when cause of action first accrued, and as such the suit is barred by limitation under Article 120 of the Limitation Act. 

 23. The learned Judges of the High Court Division erroneously decided the question of limitation and maintainability without deciding as to when the right to sue accrued. They failed to decide correctly when the cause of action arose in the present suit. Apparently it was the date on which the impugned notification was issued. 

 26. In the facts and circumstances of the case Article 120 or the Limitation Act is applicable and the period of limitation is six years. Since the plaintiffs did not file the suit within six years from the dale when the impugned notification was issued the suit was clearly barred by limitation under Article 120 of the Limitation Act.
